source_publication: Brief, independently authored paraphrases of early creator narration; original auto-caption text not redistributed.

evidence.E1: Nonfunctioning Commodore 64 board; critical ICs missing and earlier rework visible.
evidence.E2: Creator introduces the 250407 repair challenge and identifies the donated board.
evidence.E3: The device came from another retro-computing creator for assessment.
evidence.E4: Several major chips are absent, with signs of attempted previous repairs.
evidence.E5: Creator plans an assessment of the board and its other apparent problems.
evidence.E6: The opening discussion shifts toward a possibly substituted power switch.
evidence.E7: A replacement-style rocker switch is discussed; electrical equivalence has not been verified.
evidence.E8: Inspection identifies missing CPU, PLA, firmware ROM and an additional logic chip.
evidence.E9: Creator proposes examining connections and supply condition after preliminary visual work.
evidence.E10: The board has a component with superficial damage that the creator intends to inspect.
evidence.E11: Previous firmware-ROM removal appears rough, with residue around solder pads.
evidence.E12: A ceramic capacitor has a disconnected lead that may require further investigation.
evidence.E13: Previous modifications near the RF section prompt questions about trace continuity.
